text:
acme-prod-sre: Hey - since this morning our private VPC deployment started returning a lot of 429s and elevated p50/p95 latency. We've got a customer-managed gateway + nginx ingress in front of the Redwood Private control plane. Example response header: 

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" "https://private.redwood.acme/api/v1/generate"
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 6000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1680000000
{ "error": "RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED" }

acme-prod-sre: We're pretty sure it's burst traffic from a batch job but the gateway should handle bursts. Can you triage?

Aisha (support): Sorry you're seeing this — we'll dig in. Quick questions: did you recently change any ingress/gateway configs or kube autoscaler? Also is the batch job reusing the same API key or a pool?

acme-prod-sre: No changes to infra configs this week. Batch job uses one API key and spikes to ~1200 rps for ~20s every 5 minutes. Normal traffic is ~50 rps.

Jared (eng-sre): That pattern screams token-bucket exhaustion with small burst capacity. Two places to check: (1) the customer-managed gateway (nginx/Envoy/Haproxy) rate-limit plugin and burst settings, (2) Redwood Private's gateway rate limiter and per-key quotas. Could be that ingress is applying a stricter per-source IP limit or global connection limit.

Marta (eng-runtime): Also check for Redis or local quota-store saturation. Our Private deployment's ratelimiter uses a Redis backend by default — if you hit connection limits or high latency to Redis the limiter can degrade and return 429s sooner.

acme-prod-sre: Where do we find the Redwood ratelimiter config in the private bundle?

Aisha (support): In Private deployments we expose ratelimit settings in the control-plane config (config.yaml) under the gateway section. Example excerpt we usually recommend checking: 

```
gateway:
  rate_limit:
    enabled: true
    requests_per_minute: "6000"
    burst: "100"
    backend: redis
    redis_url: "redis://10.0.2.5:6379/1"
```

Aisha (support): If your batch needs short bursts, bump the "burst" and consider increasing requests_per_minute. But first confirm whether nginx ingress is applying an annotation-based limit (common for nginx-ingress v1): 

kubectl -n ingress get ingress <name> -o yaml | grep -A2 "nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-"

Typical annotations to check: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-connections, nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps, nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst.

acme-prod-sre: We have this on the ingress: 
```
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-rps: "100"
nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/limit-burst: "20"
```

acme-prod-sre: That seems low for our batch job. We put it there ages ago as a safety valve.

Jared (eng-sre): Yep, that will do it. Two options: remove/raise that ingress annotation OR add a specific path-based override for the internal batch endpoint. Also validate whether the ingress is using per-IP limits (client IP) vs per-key. If you sit behind a NAT the whole batch might appear as one IP.

acme-prod-sre: We're behind a NAT at the gateway level — yes it's a single source IP. Oof.

Marta (eng-runtime): Additional checks: 
- Inspect gateway logs for 429s and whether they're generated by nginx or by the upstream (Redwood). Example nginx log snippet: 
```
10.0.0.12 - - [15/Mar/2026:09:31:12 +0000] "POST /api/v1/generate HTTP/1.1" 429 123 "-" "curl/7.68.0" "limit_exceeded"
```
- Check Redis latency: redis-cli -h 10.0.2.5 -p 6379 --latency  or `redis-cli info clients` to see maxclients.
- Verify connection pool sizes on the gateway (worker_connections for nginx, maxconn for haproxy).

Aisha (support): Can you capture a repro with tcpdump/har or curl in the spike window and paste the full response headers? That helps us see which component emitted the 429. Also please paste the Redis INFO and the gateway pod logs for the 429 timeframe.

acme-prod-sre: Repro steps we ran: 
1) Start a simple loader from a bastion: 
```
for i in {1..1200}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -X POST https://private.redwood.acme/api/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
2) Observe 200s for first ~10s then 429s. We attached the nginx ingress logs and redis info.

infra-bot: New files uploaded: ingress-logs-1749123456.log, redis-info-1749123456.txt

Aisha (support): Thanks — logs show the 429s are returned by nginx (annotation-based limit), not Redwood. nginx returned 429 before proxying. Lines: 
```
limit_exceeded: key=route_/api/v1/generate, request=1201
```

Jared (eng-sre): OK confirmed. Action plan: 
- Short term: raise nginx annotation limit-rps to match burst characteristics (e.g., limit-rps: "1500", limit-burst: "1200") OR create a specific ingress for the batch origin with higher limits.
- Medium term: move rate-limiting responsibility to a gateway that understands per-API-key quotas (so IP-based NAT doesn't collapse many clients into one bucket). Our Private bundle's gateway can do per-key quotas when the API key is in the header and the gateway is configured with the header as the identifier.

Marta (eng-runtime): Steps to enable per-key ratelimiting on Envoy-based gateway (example): 
1) In gateway config, set `rate_limiter.identity_header: \"authorization\"` (strip Bearer prefix server-side) and enable `per_key: true`. 
2) Ensure your Redis or localstore is scaled for the expected rps. 
3) Restart gateway pods with rolling update.

Aisha (support): Also advise client-side changes: exponential backoff + jitter and connection pooling instead of 1200 parallel curl processes. Using steady concurrency (e.g., 50 concurrent with rate-limited retries) will play nicer with both ingress and backend.

acme-prod-sre: We applied a quick change to the ingress and temporarily raised limit-rps to 2000 and limit-burst to 1500. We'll monitor.

(10m later)

acme-prod-sre: After the ingress change the 429s stopped and p95 dropped back to normal. Thanks. We'll follow up to migrate to per-key limits and scale Redis.

Aisha (support): Great — please file a ticket with the exact config you want for per-key limits and we'll walk through the Private gateway change. Also note potential billing impact if you increase rate limits (higher token consumption).

Jared (eng-sre): I'll create an internal follow-up for eng-runtime to validate the per-key ratelimiter config and add a quick runbook: how to switch from IP to API-key identity and how to size Redis.

Marta (eng-runtime): Thanks, ping me on the ticket. Quick sizing tip: plan redis maxclients >= expected_concurrent_clients + 50, and set eviction policy to volatile-lru for counters. Also increase Redis TCP backlog on high load nodes.

acme-prod-sre: Appreciate the help — we'll keep you posted after the per-key rollout.

Aisha (support): Closing this support thread for now as the immediate 429s were ingress annotation limits. Reopen if it recurs after gateway changes. :thumbsup:
